http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/09/nagas.text: As Japan marks the anniversary of the 1945 atomic bombs, its leaders are pushing for a renewed debate on nuclear weapons in a challenge to the nation's long-time pacifist stance.Japan's constitution renounces offensive military force, and successive governments have maintained a decades-old pledge not to possess nuclear weapons, produce them or permit their introduction into the country.That commitment is now under pressure as East Asian neighbours — notably China — boost their military capabilities, while doubts persist about the reliability of Tokyo's biggest security backer, the United States.Japan Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has refused to clarify whether she will maintain the stance known as the three non-nuclear principles, and Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi called last month for a "discussion without a taboo" on the subject.In December, an unnamed senior administration official told local media in an off-the-record session, suggesting that Japan should possess nuclear weapons.The remark was widely reported by major Japanese outlets, including national broadcaster NHK and Asahi Shimbun, sparking public criticism."If I look at it cynically, I can't help but think that maybe she really wants to change," says Japan's anti-nuclear commitment, 82-year-old Satoshi Tanaka, a campaigner who survived the 1945 attack on Hiroshima.The country marked the 81st anniversary of the Hiroshima bombing on Thursday and will do the same on Sunday to commemorate the attack on Nagasaki.The August 1945 assault by the United States killed more than 210,000 people, including many from the effects of radiation exposure.It remains the only time that atomic weapons have been used in warfare, and was one of the last major acts of World War II.'New militarism'The Takaichi administration is undertaking a major update of the national defence strategy this year in the face of China's expanding military ambitions.The prime minister has already lifted Japan's self-imposed ban on weapons exports and expanded defence spending, while pushing to amend the constitution.Those policies have drawn rebukes from China, which accuses Japan of "new militarism" and Takaichi of bending to the whims of the far right.They have also unnerved survivors of the 1945 bombings, who have long helped shape Japan's post-war pacifist political culture.Tanaka, the Hiroshima survivor, expressed frustration that current political leaders like Takaichi are focusing on military capacity at the expense of diplomacy."There is so much talk about national security. What about building peace through diplomacy?" he said.Despite winning the 2024 Nobel Peace Prize for their efforts, they are debating whether to continue their national association as their members grow older.As of March, Japan recognised just over 91,000 survivors of the Hiroshima and Nagasaki attacks, down from over 164,000 a decade ago. Their average age is 86.7.'It only worries me'The focus has turned firmly towards the future of the non-nuclear principles, which date back to 1967.Takaichi's supporters argue that the final clause needs to be changed to allow the United States to bring nuclear arms to Japan and ensure regional deterrence.Hirofumi Yoshimura, head of the Japan Innovation Party, a coalition partner of Takaichi's government, said the principle deserved discussion in the context of the US-Japan security alliance."Of course, we need to work toward building a world without nuclear arms," Yoshimura told reporters on the anniversary of the Hiroshima bombing."But when considering how to ensure the effectiveness of extended nuclear deterrence within the framework of our alliance with the United States, I believe we should...continue to adhere to the principle of 'neither possessing nor producing' nuclear weapons," he said."As for 'not allowing them to be brought in,' I do think there is some room for discussion on that point."Critics argue that Takaichi's hawkish approach to defence increases the danger for Japan.After Takaichi attended the annual ceremony in Hiroshima on Thursday, she sat down for a televised meeting with survivors.When pressed, Takaichi declined to offer clarity on whether she might change the country's nuclear course."Our nation currently adheres to the 'three non-nuclear principles,'" she said in response to a direct question from Tanaka, without discussing what she might do next."That," Tanaka said on Friday, "only explains the current situation. It says nothing about the future."It only worries me more. I am concerned."

https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/09/18/orba.text: Menü Kereső Orbán Viktor szerint Sulyok Tamás elmenekült Belföld Aradi Hanga Zsófia Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Felkerült a YouTube-ra Orbán Viktor beszéde, amelyet a szeptember 12-i kötcsei pikniken mondott el. A volt miniszterelnök hosszú idő óta először szólalt fel a hívei előtt a zárt körű rendezvényen, ahol egy órán át értékelte a választási eredményt, a Fidesz és a KDNP „földrengésszerű vereségének” okait. A beszédje egy pontján Orbán a szuverén magyar állam védvonalainak szétveréséről beszélt. Úgy fogalmazott: „Tehát mi fölépítettünk egy nemzeti rendszert, amelynek a középpontjában a szuverén magyar állam állt. Ennek védvonalai voltak. A hatalmi rendszer az egy védvonalrendszer. Van egy szándékot megtestesítő központi akarat, amelyet védvonalak vesznek körül. Ennek a nemzeti rendszernek az első védvonala az maga az alkotmányos intézményrendszer volt. Ezt a védvonalat szétverték. Az elnök, aki ennek a védvonalnak fontos szereplője volt, elmenekült.” Orbán ezután az alkotmánybírókról beszélt, akik szintén a „nemzeti rendszer” védvonalához tartoztak. A volt kormányfő szerint köztük voltak olyanok, akik „becstelenül átálltak”, másokat eltávolították, most pedig „maradt egy-két becsületes ember, aki ott van, de már kisebbségben.” „Ezért az alkotmányos védvonalunkból az elnök is és az alkotmánybíróság is kiesett” – mondta. Magyar Péter már a választás estéjén távozásra szólította fel Sulyok Tamást. Miután Sulyok ezt nem tette meg, a tiszás többségű parlament július 13-án megszavazta azt az Alaptörvény-módosítást, ami lehetővé tette a köztársasági elnök elmozdítását. Ezt elég egyszerűen oldották meg, a módosításban az szerepelt, hogy „az Alaptörvény tizenhetedik módosításának hatálybalépését követő napon a hivatalban lévő köztársasági elnök megbízatása megszűnik.” A módosítást Sulyok Tamás végül aláírta. Sulyok az aláírásról szóló videóban arról beszélt , hogy az Alaptörvényben foglalt kötelezettségének jogi lehetőségei és lelkiismerete alapos mérlegelése után tett eleget. „Aláírásom köztársasági elnöki kötelezettségeim és a köztársasági elnöki intézmény iránt tanúsított teljes és minden körülmények közötti tiszteletem végső pecsétje” – mondta. Onnantól már nem ő volt a köztársasági elnök , feladatát ideiglenesen az Országgyűlés elnöke, Forsthoffer Ágnes vette át az új államfő, Baka András hivatalba lépéséig . Ugyanebben az Alkotmány-módosításban visszaállították az alkotmánybírák 70 éves felső korhatárát, a bírók megbízatásának hosszát pedig 12-ről 9 évre csökkentették. Ezzel automatikusan megszűnt a hetven év feletti Polt Péter és három másik alkotmánybíró megbízatása , Polt mellett Haszonicsné Ádám Mária, Juhász Miklós és Lomnici Zoltán mandátuma szűnt meg szeptember 1-jén. Még ebben a parlamenti ciklusban tölti be 70. életévét Hörcherné Marosi Ildikó, Czine Ágnes, Horváth Attila és Hende Csaba. Hende már júliusban távozott a 15 tagú testületből, helyére Sonnevend Pált , az ELTE Állam- és Jogtudományi Karának tanszékvezető egyetemi tanárát, korábbi dékánját választotta alkotmánybírónak az Országgyűlés. Szeptember 15-én az Országgyűlés öt új tagot választott a testületbe : Chronowski Nórát, Kovács András Györgyöt, Ligeti Miklóst, Orosz Árpád Gábort és Szomora Zsoltot, a Tisza Párt frakciójának jelöltjeit. https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/news/uk-.text: The devastated widow of Dave Myers has delivered a powerful response after cruel comments telling her to "stop crying". The TV chef, one half of the Hairy Bikers along with Si King, died at the age of 66 two years ago. The star finally lost his two-year battle with cancer in February 2024, leaving behind his heartbroken wife Liliana and two stepchildren. The couple had been married for 13 years, and a tribute marking his passing noted how she and her children, whom Dave "loved like his own", had brought the television personality "such happiness". Today, Liliana continues to honour his legacy through frequent Facebook updates, which she says are intended to help others dealing with grief, loss and anguish. Sharing her raw emotions and discussing the impact his death has had on her, she hopes to help those facing the same devastation. However, she has now felt compelled to respond after comments appeared on her page telling her to "get on with life" and stop "crying all over Facebook." Stating she was not there to "judge", she emphasised she wished to "make one thing clear". She explained: "My posts are not written for everyone. They are written for people who are going through one of the toughest periods of their lives. "For people living through loss. For people facing uncertainty. For people who are angry, frightened, exhausted, confused or in despair. For people trying to adjust to a life they never asked for. And most importantly, they are written from a place of grief." Liliana shared that her posts all stemmed from her own experiences which left her feeling the "kind of grief that changes you". She continued: "The kind that follows you into ordinary moments, sits beside you in silence, catches you unexpectedly and makes you realise that the life you knew no longer exists in quite the same way. "I write about grief because I live with it. I write because sometimes putting words to something is the only way I can make sense of it. Because grief has so many faces - sadness, anger, fear, guilt, loneliness, disbelief, exhaustion, even moments of peace - and none of them make the grief any less real. "I have experienced enough of it to know that there is no simple instruction to "get on with life. " You do get on with life. But you do it with grief. "You learn to carry something you never wanted to carry. You learn to live around an absence. You find a way forward without pretending that what happened didn't change you." She stressed she wasn't doing this because she wished to remain trapped in sorrow or sought sympathy - nor because she thought grief ought to shape the remainder of their existence. She continued: "I write because somewhere behind a screen there may be someone sitting alone, feeling something they cannot explain, wondering whether they are the only one who feels this way. "Maybe they need to know that someone else understands. Maybe they need words for something they haven't been able to say themselves. Maybe they simply need to be reminded that grief doesn't have a timetable, and that there is no shame in still feeling it." She concluded by pledging to continue. She said: "If my words aren't for you, that's perfectly okay. But they may be exactly what someone else needs today. And for those people, I will keep writing." Dave formed one half of the beloved Hairy Bikers culinary partnership alongside Si King. The bearded duo became renowned for journeying throughout Britain and internationally on their motorcycles, sampling and preparing regional cuisine. The pair rose to prominence while fronting The Hairy Bikers' Cookbook on BBC television, which launched with a pilot in 2005 before a complete series aired 12 months later. He met Liliana while filming Hairy Bikers in Romania for the BBC. Other programmes featured The Hairy Bikers Ride Again, The Hairy Bikers' Food Tour of Britain, The Hairy Bikers: Mums Know Best, The Hairy Bikers' Asian Adventure and Hairy Bikers: Best of British.

https://www.budapesttimes.hu/world/trump.text: The Budapest Times Trump’s Russia oil deal is a ‘massive slap in the face’ for Europe, says Czech PM The agreement between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin on the supply of Russian oil and petroleum products to the American and global markets is a massive slap in the face for Europe, Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš said at a press conference in Prague on Saturday, in response to a question from the CTK news agency. Babiš believes that Europe must respond to this step. He recalled that the agreement is all the more shocking because the American president had previously and repeatedly criticised Europe for using raw materials originating from Russia. “I understand that he (Trump) is facing elections, but for Europe this is a massive slap in the face. We’ll see what our European colleagues have to say about it,” the Czech prime minister stated, apparently alluding to the fact that an European Union summit is to take place on Thursday and Friday. “If Europe doesn’t realise that it needs to do something, this thing won’t end well,” Babiš said. Donald Trump announced on Friday that he had reached an agreement with Moscow on oil deliveries. The president has recently been attributing the rise in fuel prices in the United States to Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil refineries. He also claimed that the price increases should therefore not be explained by the Middle Eastern war, which is unpopular among Americans. “Europe is the loser of these wars (Ukraine and the Strait of Hormuz),” Czech Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economy Karel Havlíček told journalists at the press conference. In his view, it is therefore very important to pay close attention to what Trump says and does. Foreign Minister Petr Macinka, responding to a question from CTK, expressed his hope that if the Russian president is willing to sell oil, then perhaps he will also be ready to negotiate peace. Former Czech Prime Minister Petr Fiala believes that Trump’s move is merely a pre-election campaign tactic.
